acceptance_evidence: AC1, reopen returns a delivered ticket to tdd with the voided receipt hash and the reason: test_a_delivered_ticket_returns_to_tdd_on_the_next_attempt and test_the_record_carries_the_reason_and_the_commit_it_voided
AC2, a ticket that is not delivered may not be reopened, and the refusal names its stage: test_a_ticket_that_is_not_delivered_may_not_be_reopened
AC3, a merged ticket may not be reopened: test_a_merged_ticket_may_not_be_reopened merges the branch into main, pushes it, and expects the refusal
AC4, a second delivery writes a second receipt and doctor still verifies: test_a_reopened_ticket_can_be_delivered_again walks the whole cycle twice
AC5, the receipt is never edited: test_the_receipt_itself_is_untouched compares the file's bytes and its sha256 before and after

findings.claim: Record 1 of this journal names a commit that no longer exists, because start ran while the branch was accidentally based on another ticket's branch and the branch was rebased afterwards
findings.failure_scenario: A reader follows record 1's head to understand what the ticket started from and finds nothing there
findings.resolution: Recorded in the note at record 2 rather than by rewriting record 1. The underlying nuisance, that graphify's background rebuild blocks a branch switch straight after a commit, is named there too

findings.claim: Reopening could become routine and hollow out what a receipt means
findings.failure_scenario: Every ticket delivers early, gets reopened twice, and the receipt stops being evidence of anything
findings.resolution: Every reopen is a record with a reason and an actor, it is refused after merge, and SEEN-091 counts reopens as rework. The harness makes it visible rather than impossible, which is the same stance it takes on waivers

security_checklist: No new dependency: git and the standard library
No live marketplace call in a test
The command refuses after merge, so it cannot be used to rewrite history that others have pulled
